item.title: Support in the domain of numerical algorithms in the education of future secondary school mathematics teachers
item.description: arXiv:2611.06938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article presents web-based applets designed primarily to educate future mathematics teachers in the field of numerical algorithms and, secondarily, to serve high school students themselves. The applets allow users to explore the behaviour of basic numerical algorithms as applied to fundamental mathematical topics taught at high schools. The advantage is that no software is required, and students can intuitively test how a given method works by adjusting specific problem parameters, not only by viewing a list of approximate solutions, but especially through graphical output. Furthermore, they have access to multiple different methods for comparison.
item.dc:creator: Josef Dan\v{e}k

item.title: The Spectral Theory of Cographs: A Survey, Organized by Graph Matrix
item.description: arXiv:2611.06981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cographs, the $P_4$-free graphs, are exactly the graphs obtained from a single vertex by repeated disjoint union and complementation. They contain the threshold graphs, $\mathcal{C}$-graphs and form one of the primary areas for spectral graph theory. This survey is organized by matrix: after a preliminary section, there is one section for each of the adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, distance, eccentricity, Seidel, distance Laplacian and distance signless Laplacian matrices. Within each section we collect what is known for general cographs, for the subclass of $\mathcal{C}$-graphs, and where relevant, for threshold graphs. We highlight the results from the recent years, including the foundational work of Mohammadian et al., Jacobs et al., Ghorbani, Li et al., Niu et al., Lou et al., Wang at al., Mandal et al. Two structural facts are used throughout: every connected cograph has diameter at most $2$, which ties all four distance-type matrices to the adjacency and Laplacian matrices, and the partition of the vertex set into twin classes is equitable for every one of the eight matrices, giving a uniform description of each spectrum (for the Laplacian this is the twin-reduction theory of Barik--Reddy, which we present in detail). Besides surveying the literature, we record several consequences, and mark them as such: an exact decomposition of the eccentricity matrix of a connected cograph, yielding an eigenvalue-free interval for the eccentricity spectrum of all connected cographs; the full distance Laplacian spectrum and its extremal eigenvalues; an eigenvalue-free interval for the distance signless Laplacian valid for every connected graph of diameter at most $2$; an interlacing theorem tying the distance spectrum to the adjacency spectrum. A comparison table across all eight matrices and a list of open problems close the paper.
item.dc:creator: Pallabi Manna, Santanu Mandal, Fernando C. Tura

item.title: Early career researcher responses to AI in math
item.description: arXiv:2610.40584v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We've heard a lot about AI in math from Fields medalists, AI labs, and established professors. However, the personal stakes are highest for early career researchers. Hoping to provide a platform for graduate students and postdocs to voice their opinions, concerns, and experiences, we wrote and distributed a survey on AI in math. In this article, we share the responses to our survey. All responses are anonymous, and respondents came from almost $60$ institutions and at least $5$ countries. Our survey included both multiple choice questions and more open-ended free response questions. If you are a senior mathematician or university administrator reading these survey results, our goal is for you to understand the concerns of the younger generations and use your authority to take action accordingly. If you are an early career mathematician reading these survey results, we hope you find comfort in the knowledge that your experiences are shared by many others. If you are not a mathematician, we hope you come away from this article with a deeper understanding of the goals, values, and concerns of the community.
item.dc:creator: Anna Brandenberger, Hanna Mularczyk, Dora Woodruff
